modbus_existing_node.title: Existing Modbus Node
modbus_existing_node.description: Select an existing Modbus hub defined in Home Assistant

modbus_usb.title: Modbus – USB port (serial)
modbus_usb.description: Modbus serial (USB / RS485) connection settings. The device supports only 9600, 19200 and 38400 baud.

power_meter_settings.title: Power Meter settings
power_meter_settings.description: Select the Modbus Node used by this Power Meter and set its Modbus ID. All values are read with a single Modbus packet.

device_type.title: Device type
device_type.description: Select the type of device you want to add

power_meter_device_info.title: Device parameters
power_meter_device_info.description:
The following parameters were read from the device:

- **Model:** {model} (register 0x0000 = {model_code})

- **Voltage range:** {voltage_range} (register 0x0002)

- **Current range:** {current_range} (register 0x0003)

Confirm to add the device.

power_meter_phases.title: Phase assignment
power_meter_phases.description: Assign a voltage phase to each current channel of {model}. The current setting read from the device is shown; confirming writes any changes to the device.

tools_device.title: Tools – current device
tools_device.description:
Enter the Modbus ID the device currently uses (factory default: ID 1, 9600 baud, 8N1). The connection entered in the previous steps must match the device's current communication settings.

**Broadcast write:** the new settings are sent to ID 0 and are received by **ALL devices on the bus**. If more devices share the bus, their ID and communication settings will change as well – use it only when exactly one device is connected.

data.modbus_device_id: Current Modbus ID of the device

tools_new_params.title: Tools – new communication settings
tools_new_params.description: Set the ID and the communication parameters to be written to the device. The new ID must not be used by another device on the same bus.

tools_confirm.title: Tools – confirm

tools_connection_type.title: Tools – connection to the device
tools_connection_type.description: Choose HOW you connect to the device whose settings you want to change. The following windows describe its CURRENT communication parameters – the new parameters are entered in a later step.

tools_existing_node.title: Tools – existing Modbus Node
tools_existing_node.description: Select the existing Modbus hub defined in Home Assistant that the device is connected through. Speed and format are determined by this hub (the device's CURRENT settings).

tools_usb.title: Tools – CURRENT device settings (USB / RS485)
tools_usb.description: Enter the CURRENT communication parameters of the device, i.e. the ones it uses RIGHT NOW (factory setting: 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit). The new parameters to be written to the device are entered in the next step.

tools_tcp.title: Tools – connection via TCP server
tools_tcp.description: Enter the address of the TCP gateway the device is connected through. The RS485 speed and format are determined by the gateway – they are not entered here.

tools_udp.title: Tools – connection via UDP server
tools_udp.description: Enter the address of the UDP gateway the device is connected through. The RS485 speed and format are determined by the gateway – they are not entered here.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot read the device. Check the Modbus Node, Modbus ID and wiring.
error.no_modbus_nodes: No Modbus nodes were found in the system. Define at least one Modbus hub first.
error.no_serial_ports: No free serial ports were found. All ports may already be in use.
error.no_modbus_node_entries: No Modbus Node device exists. Create at least one Modbus Node device first.
error.device_id_in_use: A Power Meter with this Modbus ID already exists on the selected Modbus Node.
error.node_not_loaded: The selected Modbus Node is not loaded. Check the Modbus Node device.
error.write_failed: Cannot write the settings to the device. Check the Modbus Node, Modbus ID and wiring.
error.phase_invalid_value: The device contains an invalid phase assignment for some channels (a value other than A, B or C). Phase A is shown for them; submitting writes the selection to the device.
error.write_verify_failed: The device did not accept the settings: the values read back after writing differ from the written ones.
error.tools_no_change: The new settings are the same as the current ones.

abort.tools_applied:
Done. The device now responds with: ID **{new_id}**, **{new_baud}** baud, **{new_format}**.

Set the same serial parameters (baud rate, parity, stop bits) on the Modbus Node used by this device – or on the TCP/UDP gateway – and, if the device is used as a Power Meter, set the new Modbus ID in the Power Meter configuration.
abort.tools_pending: The device acknowledged the settings, but it still responds with the OLD settings (ID {old_id}, {old_baud} baud, {old_format}). The new settings may take effect only after the device is power-cycled. Restart it and then use: ID {new_id}, {new_baud} baud, {new_format}.
abort.tools_unreachable: The device responds neither with the old nor with the new settings, so the result could not be verified. The settings may have been applied – try the new ones (ID {new_id}, {new_baud} baud, {new_format}). If the device cannot be reached at all, try the factory defaults: ID 1, 9600 baud, 8N1.
abort.tools_unverified: The settings were sent (ID {new_id}, {new_baud} baud, {new_format}). Over this kind of connection (TCP/UDP or an existing Modbus hub) a change of the baud rate or data format cannot be verified, because the link settings are fixed. Set the same serial parameters on the gateway / Modbus hub and check that the device responds.
